chunks: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made the sustenance of the believers from where they do not reckon,
and that is because when a servant does not know the direction of his sustenance, his supplication increases.

key_terms.أَرْزَاقَ: Sustenance/provisions — rizq is a broad concept in Islamic theology encompassing all that God grants a person for their living
key_terms.حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُونَ: From where they do not reckon — an echo of Quran 65:3, signifying divine provision beyond human expectation
key_terms.دُعَاء: Supplication — du'a, the act of beseeching God; here presented as the spiritual fruit of uncertainty about one's rizq
key_terms.وَجْهَ رِزْقِهِ: The direction/means of his sustenance — the channels through which his provision comes

ai.seo_question: Where does God provide sustenance for the believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that God provides for believers from unexpected sources. This hadith belongs to a chapter in al-Kafi addressing the believer's relationship with livelihood (rizq). The theological implication is that divine providence operates beyond human calculation, and the spiritual benefit is that uncertainty over sustenance drives the believer toward increased supplication and reliance on God.
